compositionRules.assert: Submit trigger must render a Form.Item with htmlType="submit" placed after all data fields, not interleaved
No two sibling input fields should share the same name prop within a single Form instance
Form fields should not be nested inside a Card with no label; the field-annotator relationship is lost for assistive tech

bad: <Form><Form.Item name="email" label="Email"><Input /></Form.Item></Form> where onFinish is omitted so the entered data never gets validated or captured
<Button htmlType="submit" /> placed above the first field, breaking top-to-bottom read order before submit
<Form><Form.Item><Input /></Form.Item><Form.Item><Input /></Form.Item></Form> with no name on any item, so values are unreachable on submit
Using plain <input> elements directly inside <Form.Item> instead of an antd input component, losing validation binding and field-annotator wiring
A form with required fields but no rules on those items, so the required asterisk is purely decorative
good: <Form layout="vertical" onFinish={handleSubmit}><Form.Item name="email" label="Email" rules={[{ required: true }]}><Input /></Form.Item><Form.Item><Button type="primary" htmlType="submit">Submit</Button></Form.Item></Form>
<Form.Item name="username" label="Username" rules={[{ required: true, message: 'Please enter username' }]}><Input /></Form.Item>

hardRules.message: A Form must declare an onFinish handler; without it the entered data is not captured on a successful validation pass.
Every Form must contain at least one submit trigger (Form.Item wrapping a Button with htmlType="submit") so the user can complete the entry.
Each Form.Item that wraps an input must have a name prop so its value is reachable in the onFinish values object.

hardRules.expr: not exists slot.fields descendant of type Form
hardRules.message: A Form must not be nested inside another Form; field binding and submission scope become ambiguous.

meaning.definition: A structured input container that collects a set of related user-supplied values, drives field-level validation, and yields a typed values object to the system once all constraints are satisfied.
doNotUseWhen: Displaying read-only data, single confirm actions, or navigation - use Alert/Modal/Menu instead.
Capturing a single immediate action rather than a record - use a standalone Button or Switch.
Presenting tabular existing data without editing - use Table.
Filtering or searching a dataset - prefer a compact search/filter bar unless a multi-field record is genuinely being created.
useWhen: The user is creating or editing a structured record with two or more logically related fields.
The system must validate one or more inputs before committing them as a coherent unit.
Submission should only fire after all required fields pass validation, producing a single values payload.

layout.description: Arrangement axis for label/control pairs: horizontal (label left), vertical (label above), or inline (single row, compact).

onFinish.description: Function invoked only after all field validations pass, receiving the finished values object as its sole argument. Required so entered data is actually captured.
onFinish.requiredWhen: form has at least one submit trigger

onFinishFailed.description: Function invoked when submission is attempted but one or more fields fail validation, receiving the error info.

requiredMark.description: Whether to render the required-field asterisk marker. Must stay true when any field declares a required rule.

rules: Each field should be wrapped by a Form.Item so its value and validation participate in onFinish.
At least one Form.Item should host a submit Button (htmlType="submit") at the bottom of the form.
Must be a single Button with htmlType="submit", typically type="primary", placed as the last field row.

softRules: Prefer layout="vertical" on long or unfamiliar forms so labels stay readable on narrow viewports.
Always provide a meaningful message on required-field rules so failed validation gives actionable feedback.
Place the primary submit button at the bottom-right of the form, with any secondary/reset action to its left.
Group semantically related fields with the headings/section affordance rather than one flat list when there are 7+ fields.

semantics.horizontal: Label aligned to the left of its control; best for wide forms on desktop.
semantics.inline: All fields and the submit action collapsed onto a single row; best for compact, single-action bars like quick filters.
semantics.vertical: Label stacked above its control; best for long or narrow-view forms and accessible label pairing.
